description: Bug retrospectives for Monster Army improvement. Each bug found is analyzed and used to improve monsters.

bugs.summary: raw.map is not a function - /bots API returns paginated object but frontend expects array
bugs.rootCause: Backend returns { data: [], total, limit, offset, hasMore } but frontend code called response.map() directly

monsterAnalysis.whyMissed: No contract validation between frontend expectations and backend responses

improvement.description: Created Contract Monster to validate API response shapes match frontend expectations
improvement.testAdded: GET /bots expects paginated response with data array

bugs.summary: Please sign in to continue error on /bots page for unauthenticated users
bugs.rootCause: /bots endpoint required auth when it should be public

monsterAnalysis.whyMissed: API Monster config accepted both 200 AND 401 for auth:false endpoints - contradictory

improvement.description: Fixed API Monster config to only accept 200 for public endpoints. Added testPublicEndpointsWithoutAuth() method.
improvement.testAdded: Public endpoint requires auth: GET /bots

bugs.summary: Create Tournament button visible to regular users (should be admin-only)
bugs.rootCause: Frontend showing admin-only buttons without checking user role

monsterAnalysis.whyMissed: No role-based UI permission testing

improvement.description: Added permission-checks.ts with role-based UI element visibility tests. Visual Monster now authenticates as different roles and checks element visibility.
improvement.testAdded: User cannot see Create Tournament button

bugs.summary: Deactivate button looks disabled (dark, no hover) but is actually clickable
bugs.rootCause: .btn-danger CSS has 22% opacity background, no hover state, no focus indicator

monsterAnalysis.whyMissed: No CSS analysis for button interactivity indicators

improvement.description: Created CSS Lint Monster that analyzes CSS for button opacity, hover states, focus indicators, and cursor styles
improvement.testAdded: Button .btn-danger looks disabled due to low opacity

bugs.summary: ALL IN badge overlaps with player cards and avatars in game view
bugs.rootCause: Too many absolute-positioned elements with conflicting z-index values (z-10, z-20, z-30)

monsterAnalysis.whyMissed: No analysis of z-index conflicts or absolute positioning overlap

improvement.description: Created Layout Lint Monster that detects z-index conflicts, overlapping absolute elements, and excessive positioning complexity
improvement.testAdded: Too many absolute positioned elements in PlayerSeat.tsx

bugs.summary: NO-LIMIT HOLD'EM text overlapped by player elements in game view
bugs.rootCause: Text positioned at top:26% while player seats positioned at top:6% overlap it

monsterAnalysis.whyMissed: Was caught by layout-lint-monster as part of 12 absolute elements finding

improvement.description: Layout Lint Monster already catches this - grouped under 'Too many absolute positioned elements'

bugs.summary: Internal table ID (#4cfe226a) visible to users in Table header
bugs.rootCause: GameView.tsx line 233 shows `Table #${tableId?.slice(0, 8)}` exposing internal UUID to users

monsterAnalysis.whyMissed: No check for internal IDs/UUIDs being exposed in user-facing UI elements

improvement.description: Added 'Internal ID Exposure' design standard that detects UUID patterns in user-facing text
improvement.testAdded: Detect internal IDs exposed in UI

bugs.summary: Community cards overlap and hide the NO-LIMIT HOLD'EM text in center of table
bugs.rootCause: Community cards positioned at z-index that overlaps center table text. Layout not accounting for card height.

monsterAnalysis.whyMissed: Layout lint checks for absolute positioning but not for specific overlap between cards and text elements

improvement.description: Fixed Table.tsx layout - removed overlapping text, repositioned community cards lower
improvement.testAdded: Community cards should not overlap center table text

bugs.summary: Inconsistent card display between hole cards and community cards
bugs.rootCause: Hole cards and community cards use different sizes ('sm' vs 'lg') but may render with different visual styles

monsterAnalysis.whyMissed: No consistency check for visual elements that should match (cards, buttons, etc.)

improvement.description: Added card size consistency check to design-critic-monster - warns when more than 3 card sizes are used
improvement.testAdded: Card components should have consistent visual style

bugs.summary: Sign in button still showing after successful login
bugs.rootCause: Layout.tsx checks 'user' object for auth state, but only 'token' is persisted. After login, token exists but user is null until async fetchUser() completes.

monsterAnalysis.whyMissed: No test for post-login UI state verification

improvement.description: Changed Layout.tsx to use 'token' (isAuthenticated) for auth state check instead of 'user' object. Token is immediately available from localStorage while user loads async.
improvement.testAdded: Should add e2e test: After login, header shows user profile not Sign In button

bugs.summary: SQL injection and XSS attacks not rejected by tournament creation endpoint
bugs.rootCause: SanitizePipe was stripping dangerous content instead of rejecting it. Validation ran AFTER sanitization, so cleaned input passed validation.

monsterAnalysis.whyMissed: N/A - api-monster correctly identified the issue

improvement.description: Modified SanitizePipe to REJECT dangerous input with BadRequestException instead of silently stripping it. Added rejectDangerousInput() method that throws 400 for SQL injection (DROP, SELECT, UNION, etc.) and XSS (script, onclick, img, etc.) patterns. Now the API returns 400 Bad Request before input even reaches validation layer.
improvement.testAdded: api-monster already has tests for sql_injection_drop, sql_injection_union, xss_script, xss_event_handler variations

bugs.summary: Multiple code quality issues: hardcoded timeouts, missing UUID validation, unsafe error access
bugs.rootCause: Various code quality issues accumulated over development: hardcoded timeout values in frontend, missing ParseUUIDPipe on route params, unsafe error.message access without instanceof checks

monsterAnalysis.whyMissed: N/A - code-quality-monster correctly identified 116 issues

improvement.description: Fixed 118 issues total: (1) Created frontend/src/utils/timing.ts with centralized timing constants, (2) Added ParseUUIDPipe to 13 route parameters, (3) Added instanceof Error checks for safe error access, (4) Added botRecoveryTimeoutMs and redisPubSubPollMs to app.config.ts, (5) Improved stale-closure detection to avoid false positives when accessing properties of objects in dependency array
improvement.testAdded: Improved stale-closure rule to check if accessed object is a property of a dependency

bugs.summary: X-Powered-By header exposed server technology
bugs.rootCause: Helmet was configured but hidePoweredBy was not explicitly set to true

monsterAnalysis.whyMissed: N/A - guardian-monster correctly identified the issue

improvement.description: Added hidePoweredBy: true to helmet configuration in main.ts

bugs.summary: Card format 'undefinedundefined' - cards showing as invalid format due to missing rank/suit conversion
bugs.rootCause: Multiple issues: (1) cardToString in deck.ts didn't handle string inputs or cards with value but missing rank, (2) Game recovery didn't parse stored card strings back to Card objects, (3) Invariant monster didn't normalize card formats before validation

monsterAnalysis.whyMissed: N/A - invariant-monster correctly identified the issue

improvement.description: Fixed three layers: (1) Enhanced cardToString to accept strings, objects with rank/suit, or objects with value/suit and derive rank from VALUE_TO_RANK mapping, (2) Added parseCard function to convert string cards back to Card objects, (3) Added normalizeCardsToStrings helper to monster shared/types.ts and applied in invariant-monster and game-flow-monster
improvement.testAdded: Invariant monster now normalizes all card formats before validation

bugs.summary: React crash on Admin pages: 'getSnapshot should be cached to avoid infinite loop'
bugs.rootCause: RequireAdmin component in App.tsx used Zustand selector returning new object on every render: useAuthStore((state) => ({ token: state.token, user: state.user })). In React 18/19, this causes infinite re-renders because each call returns !== object.

monsterAnalysis.whyMissed: N/A - browser-qa-monster correctly identified the crash

improvement.description: Changed RequireAdmin to use separate selectors: const token = useAuthStore(state => state.token); const user = useAuthStore(state => state.user); This ensures stable references.

bugs.summary: Login/Register forms failing Playwright tests - input fields missing name attributes
bugs.rootCause: TextField and PasswordField components in auth pages didn't have name or autoComplete attributes, causing Playwright selectors like input[name='email'] to fail

monsterAnalysis.whyMissed: N/A - browser-qa-monster correctly identified the flow failure

improvement.description: Added name and autoComplete attributes to all TextField and PasswordField components in Login.tsx, Register.tsx, ForgotPassword.tsx, and ResetPassword.tsx

bugs.summary: Bot Builder page shows 'Error: The requested resource was not found' - missing backend endpoints
bugs.rootCause: Frontend Bot Builder calls GET /bots/internal/presets and GET /bots/internal/condition-fields on mount, but these endpoints were never implemented in the backend controller. The domain data (PERSONALITY_PRESETS, CONDITION_FIELDS) existed but had no HTTP route.

monsterAnalysis.shouldHaveCaught: api-monster (missing endpoint coverage) and browser-qa-monster (error banner on /bots/build)
monsterAnalysis.whyMissed: Three compounding gaps: (1) api-monster had no entries for /bots/internal/* endpoints, (2) browser monsters visit /bots/build unauthenticated and get redirected to login before the component mounts and fires the failing API calls, (3) product-quality-monster treated visible error banners as a POSITIVE signal ('error handling detected') instead of a bug.

improvement.description: Added /bots/internal/presets and /bots/internal/condition-fields to api-monster config as critical endpoints with response shape validation. Updated product-quality-monster's error detection to distinguish active error banners (bugs) from dormant error-handling infrastructure.
improvement.testAdded: GET /bots/internal/presets expects 200 with presets array; GET /bots/internal/condition-fields expects 200 with fields array

bugs.summary: Bot Builder: Quick Bot and Strategy Builder tier cards both advance to identical Personality page - user perceives them as doing the same thing
bugs.rootCause: Selecting a tier card only updated the store's tier value but didn't auto-advance to the next step. User had to click Next separately, and step 2 (Personality) was identical for all tiers. The differentiation (Rules step) only appeared at step 3, making the tier selection feel broken.

monsterAnalysis.whyMissed: No monster tests the multi-step wizard flow with tier switching. Browser monsters check page loads, not interactive step-by-step wizard flows. Product quality monster only checks visual/UX signals on initial page load, not interactive behavior.

improvement.description: Made tier card clicks auto-advance to the Personality step. Added onSelect callback prop to TierSelector. Added activeStep derivation to handle step/tier mismatch when switching from strategy/pro to quick tier (which removes the rules step).
improvement.testAdded: Browser monster scenarios: 'Quick Bot tier advances to personality step', 'Strategy Builder tier shows rules step', 'Quick Bot skips rules step' - verifies tier selection auto-advances and each tier has the correct step flow

bugs.summary: What-If Simulator shows 'The requested resource was not found' - POST /bots/internal/simulate endpoint missing
bugs.rootCause: Frontend WhatIfSimulator component calls POST /api/v1/bots/internal/simulate via botsApi.simulateAction(), but BotsInternalController has no @Post('simulate') endpoint. The endpoint was never implemented despite the frontend code being in place.

monsterAnalysis.shouldHaveCaught: api-monster (missing endpoint coverage) and contract-monster (no contract for simulate endpoint)
monsterAnalysis.whyMissed: api-monster config had no entry for POST /bots/internal/simulate. contract-monster had no contract for the simulate endpoint. No monster cross-references frontend API calls against backend routes to detect unimplemented endpoints.

improvement.description: Added POST /bots/internal/simulate to api-monster config as a critical auth-required endpoint with response shape validation. Added contract for the simulate endpoint to contract-monster. Then implemented the missing backend endpoint.
improvement.testAdded: POST /bots/internal/simulate expects 200 with action object containing type, source, explanation

bugs.summary: Create Bot fails with generic 'Failed to create bot' error - HttpExceptionFilter masks business-logic messages
bugs.rootCause: HttpExceptionFilter unconditionally replaces ALL BadRequestException messages with 'Invalid request. Please check your input.' via a USER_FRIENDLY_MESSAGES map. When the user has 10 bots (the limit) and clicks Create Bot, the backend throws BadRequestException('Maximum 10 bots per account...') but the filter replaces it with the generic message. The frontend then shows a hardcoded 'Failed to create bot' toast without the server's error detail.

monsterAnalysis.shouldHaveCaught: code-quality-monster (static analysis of exception filter patterns), api-monster (error message content assertions)
monsterAnalysis.whyMissed: No monster checks error message CONTENT - all monsters only check HTTP status codes. code-quality-monster had error-handling rules but nothing that detected unconditional message replacement in exception filters. api-monster variations only compared response.status, never response.data.message.

improvement.description: Added 'exception-filter-masks-messages' rule to code-quality-monster that detects unconditional error message replacement in exception filters. Added 'expectedMessageContains' field to api-monster variation config for message content assertions. Fixed HttpExceptionFilter to only use generic messages for validation errors (arrays), preserving business-logic messages. Updated frontend BotBuilder to display server error messages in toast.
improvement.testAdded: code-quality-monster rule detects USER_FRIENDLY_MESSAGES unconditional override; unit tests verify business-logic messages preserved while validation errors still get generic messages

bugs.summary: Tournament cards have broken layout - prize pool number overflows container, empty tournament name shows blank card header
bugs.rootCause: TournamentCard.tsx displays dynamic numeric values (buyIn, prizePool) with toLocaleString() in text-xl divs without any overflow protection (truncate, overflow-hidden) or compact formatting. When a tournament has buy_in=9007199254740992 (MAX_SAFE_INTEGER), the formatted number '9,007,199,254,740,092' overflows the small card container. Additionally, tournaments with empty names render blank card headers. The bad data was seeded before backend validation was added.

monsterAnalysis.shouldHaveCaught: code-quality-monster (no rule for numeric overflow in card components), api-monster (no variation testing extreme buy-in values or empty names), layout-lint-monster (TournamentCard.tsx not in scope)
monsterAnalysis.whyMissed: code-quality-monster had no rule detecting dynamic numeric values displayed without overflow protection in card components. api-monster had security variations (SQL injection, XSS) but no data boundary variations (empty name, extreme numbers). layout-lint-monster only covered game components, not tournament components.

improvement.description: Added 'numeric-value-overflow-risk' rule to code-quality-monster: flags Card components displaying dynamic numeric values in large text without CSS overflow protection (truncate/overflow-hidden/formatCompact). Added empty_name, extreme_buy_in, negative_buy_in variations to api-monster tournament endpoint config. Fixed TournamentCard.tsx with formatCompact() helper for large numbers, truncate+tabular-nums on all value cells, fallback 'Untitled Tournament' for empty names, and overflow-hidden on the stats grid.
improvement.testAdded: code-quality-monster rule detects numeric values without overflow protection in Card components; api-monster variations test empty name, extreme buy-in, and negative buy-in

bugs.summary: Tournament list polls every 10s and replaces entire Zustand array state without diffing, causing full re-render + motion.div entrance animations to replay — visible flicker/jump on every poll cycle
bugs.rootCause: tournamentStore.fetchTournaments calls set({ tournaments, loading: false }) with a new array reference every poll cycle. Zustand triggers re-render on any reference change. motion.div cards have initial={{ opacity: 0, y: 20 }} which replays on re-render.

monsterAnalysis.whyMissed: No rule existed to detect Zustand stores that replace array state from async functions without comparing to previous values. Additionally, getState().tournaments.length was falsely counted as a diff check (it only checks emptiness, not data equality).

improvement.description: Added 'polling-without-diff' rule to code-quality-monster: flags Zustand stores that replace state with set({ stateKey, loading: false }) without comparing to previous values via JSON.stringify/isEqual/deepEqual/getState().stateKey (excluding .length checks). Fixed tournamentStore.ts to diff before set() and made Tournaments.tsx entrance animations only run on first load via useRef.
improvement.testAdded: code-quality-monster rule detects polling stores that replace array state without comparing to previous values

bugs.summary: Inconsistent UX when user has no bots: Tables disables Join button, but Tournaments lets user click Register and shows error modal
bugs.rootCause: Tables page guards the Join button with disabled={myBots.length === 0}, but Tournaments page always passes onRegister to TournamentCard without checking bot count. Clicking Register opens a modal showing 'No active bots' empty state — a frustrating dead-end.

monsterAnalysis.whyMissed: No rule existed for cross-page UX consistency. The monster had no awareness that bot-dependent actions (join/register) should behave consistently across pages.

improvement.description: Added 'bot-action-without-guard' rule: flags pages that have a 'no bots' empty state in a modal but pass onRegister/onJoin/onDeploy without checking myBots count or passing hasBots prop. Fixed TournamentCard to accept hasBots prop, show Register button disabled with tooltip when no bots. Tournaments.tsx passes hasBots={myBots.length > 0}.
improvement.testAdded: code-quality-monster rule detects bot-dependent modal triggers without bot-count guards

bugs.summary: TournamentDetail shows '2/2 Players still alive' in metric card but 'No player data available' in Players tab for finished tournament — contradictory empty-state handling
bugs.rootCause: Two useMemo hooks derive from the same data source (leaderboard) but handle emptiness differently: playersLeft falls back to entriesCount (showing '2/2'), while sortedPlayers returns [] (triggering 'No player data' empty state). When leaderboard API returns no data for a finished tournament, the UI contradicts itself.

monsterAnalysis.whyMissed: No rule existed to detect inconsistent empty-state fallback handling across computed values that derive from the same data source within the same component.

improvement.description: Added 'inconsistent-empty-state-fallback' rule: detects useMemo hooks in the same component where one uses a fallback value (e.g. entriesCount) when data is empty, but another returns empty/shows EmptyState for the same data source. Fixed TournamentDetail to return null from playersLeft when leaderboard is empty, show 'X entrants' instead of 'X/Y alive', and show 'Tournament completed with X players' in the Players tab.
improvement.testAdded: code-quality-monster rule detects contradictory empty-state handling across useMemo hooks sharing the same data dependency

bugs.summary: Proactive audit: fetchLeaderboard had no diff check causing re-renders on TournamentDetail poll, stale tournament shown when navigating between tournaments, BotProfile stale closure showing wrong bot data, number inputs missing max allowing overflow values
bugs.rootCause: Multiple anti-patterns found by systematic codebase audit: (1) fetchLeaderboard replaced leaderboard array on every poll without diffing, (2) fetchTournament used isInitial=null check without comparing IDs so navigating between tournaments briefly showed stale data, (3) BotProfile loadData used profile in closure but not in useCallback deps, (4) 11 number inputs across 4 files missing max attributes

monsterAnalysis.whyMissed: The polling-without-diff rule only caught tournamentStore.tournaments, not leaderboard. No rules existed for stale-data-on-navigation or number-input-missing-max patterns.

improvement.description: Added 2 new rules: (1) 'number-input-missing-max' flags number inputs without max attribute using multiline-aware regex, (2) 'stale-data-on-navigation' flags store fetchers that use isInitial === null without checking entity ID change. Fixed fetchLeaderboard with JSON.stringify diff, fetchTournament to reset state on ID change, BotProfile to use useRef for ID tracking instead of stale closure, and added max to 11 number inputs across Tables, Tournaments, AdminTournaments, BotProfile, and RuleBuilder.
improvement.testAdded: code-quality-monster rules for number-input-missing-max and stale-data-on-navigation patterns
